title: use_shrink_chi=true silently does nothing when use_shrink_abfs=false
symptom: A finite-T Na bcc run with use_shrink_chi=true but use_shrink_abfs=false actually executed the un-shrunk, complex, kBLACS path; the static chi for the selected ABF pair did not come from a shrunk (sinvS) path, so any shrink-based attribution of that static chi was wrong.
root_cause: LibRPA decides shrinkage from whether sinvS is non-empty, and sinvS is only loaded when use_shrink_abfs=true (shrink entry driver/read_data.cpp:713, complex selection src/core/chi0.cpp:961, actual call src/core/chi0.cpp:2190). use_shrink_chi is subordinate, so setting it alone is a no-op.
minimal_fix: Set use_shrink_abfs=true (so sinvS is loaded) whenever use_shrink_chi=true or a shrunk auxiliary basis is intended; otherwise record in the log that the run is un-shrunk.
validation: Confirm from the driver/reader log that sinvS was loaded and the shrink branch at driver/read_data.cpp:713 is taken before attributing any result to shrinkage.
avoid: Do not assume use_shrink_chi=true implies shrinkage, and do not compare shrunk vs un-shrunk results from input flags alone - the flags are not the mechanism.

parameters.use_shrink_chi: effective only when sinvS is non-empty
parameters.shrink_switch_mechanism: non-empty sinvS, not the use_shrink_chi flag
